grievance: the road shoulder is invincible: holding one key pins the car just past lane 3's collision envelope, so my hold-right run sat there 25s for 1107m without traffic ever touching it - once you know the trick the game cannot be lost
change: roadside clamp moved from 4px to 16px inside the painted edge on both sides, so the car can no longer ride the white line outside the outermost lanes' collision envelope; every lane now carries real crash risk
proof: the same hold-right-for-25s play that ended 1107m in untouched now crashes at 280m after 7.7s, while honest weaving runs still reach 2107m/41s - the longest run observed either way - so survival finally demands steering, not knowing a trick

grievance: the game is utterly silent: an instrumented drive of version 1 never constructed a single AudioContext from title to crash to restart, so the speed ramp I could feel building had no voice and the crash that ended my hold-right run at 213m landed without a sound
change: synthesised Web Audio, nothing else touched: a lazy AudioContext created on first gesture feeds a two-oscillator engine (sawtooth over a square sub through a lowpass) whose pitch sweeps ~65-120 Hz per gear of the speed ramp so each 80 px/s of acceleration audibly climbs then drops back; crashing cuts that engine near-instantly and fires a decaying filtered-noise crunch with a 150->38 Hz sine thump underneath; reset fades it all out. Every node is guarded so a missing or blocked AudioContext leaves the game exactly as playable as before, just silent
proof: playing version 2, one context comes up running on the Start click where version 1 created none, and the engine pitch measured live under my own driving climbs 68.9 -> 74 -> 79.3 -> 84.5 -> 89.4 Hz across five seconds of play and reads 95.3 Hz by 268m - the ramp is now audible, not only felt; the same hold-right crash adds a buffer noise source plus thump oscillator while the engine gain drops to 0 within ~0.7s, Space restarts into a fresh engine pair (66.6/33.3 Hz) without reloading, and reset() returns to title with everything faded out

grievance: the road is a treadmill: my best weave run covered 3654m over 67s and the strip under me was pixel-for-pixel the one I started on - instrumented, the car sat at exactly x=240 with 0px of lateral motion whenever I let go, because there is literally nowhere to go: no bends, bare flat verges, nothing on the horizon but the same three lanes and grey boxes, so a 3000m drive looks identical to a 100m one
change: the highway finally goes somewhere: the centreline is now a pure function of world distance - two layered sines whose long lazy sweeps alternate with tighter bends - and everything hangs off it, so lane dashes, painted edges, verges and traffic all follow the curve (collisions moved to road coordinates: lateral offset plus nose-to-tail gap, which stays true through a bend where screen-x would lie); centrifugal drift pushes the car toward the outside of a bend in proportion to slope times speed - negligible at 220 px/s, a shove near 75 px/s at top speed you must counter-steer; delineator posts every 150px hug both edges and two staggered hash-scattered strands of verge trees stream past, with clearings, so the forest is stable while the road moves under it. Shift 1's 16px shoulder clamp survives unchanged as the u-space limit
proof: hands-off, the version-2 car never left x=240 for its whole 200m life; hands-off in this version the car slid across 15px of road (x 280..295) with no input as the bend carried and shoved it - the world moves you now, not just the keys; the same canvas-reading driver bot that managed 474m/12s on straight v2 in this session threaded the bends for 2159m/41.7s here, so long runs survive but passive ones die fast; the probe's mid-play shot shows the tarmac sweeping right between trees and posts where every earlier version's shot could have been mistaken for the seed; engine audio still tracks the ramp and Enter-restart plus reset() still land clean without a reload

grievance: surviving was the only thing that scored, so the winning way to play was timid: an instrumented drive of version 3 tracked 132 overtakes in a single run, two dozen of them inside half a car's width, and not one touched the score - the HUD just counted metres, so threading a gap and giving it a wide berth paid exactly the same
change: close-pass scoring: when a car's nose crosses my tail I am judged on lateral clearance in road coordinates - under 20px pays 20-100 points scaled by how little room was left, and close passes inside three seconds chain into a multiplier up to x5, shown as a live 'chain' bar under the score; each pass pops its value where it happened; the HUD keeps points and metres, survival still pays its base 1 pt/m, and the crash report reads 'metres, close passes, best chain'; title copy teaches the rule
proof: driving version 4, the same brave line now visibly outscores the safe one: a seeded harness pushing real key events through update() watched popups land as +48, then +108 x2, +174 x3, +212 x4, +300 x5 - payouts climbing with the chain and capping at x5 - while an unseeded browser run I steered by sight ended '2397 points / 1397 m, 12 close passes, best chain x5', roughly double what those metres alone would have paid in version 3; contact still ends the run (the graze bot died mid-chain more than once), Space restart and reset() come back clean without a reload, and the engine and crash audio are untouched

grievance: the driver still has exactly one verb: instrumented drives of version 7 show forward pace is a metronome I cannot touch - my dist trace climbs on rails at the same ~7 m per 200 ms whether I am threading gaps or holding dead centre, and state() has no way to even report speed because nothing on screen or in the API can change it; a dense wave of traffic is therefore not a situation, only a coin-flip over which lane to die in, and the run's one decision (which side to slide) stops paying past the first minute

grievance: the scoring loop is mute: nine passes built a language nobody can hear - a tight shave pays up to 100 points and chains multiply that five-fold, yet in every drive of version 9 I made (hands-off to 394 m, weaving runs, brake-and-shave attempts) the only sounds from first gesture to crash were the pass-2 engine drone and the pass-2 crash crunch; my instrumented drives confirmed it - nothing in the code path of an overtake, a chain ringing up or a chain starving out so much as constructs an oscillator, so a 500-point chained shave lands as quietly as the empty road beside you and you play the whole risk-reward game by eye alone
change: four synthesised voices for the run's own language, all through the existing lazily-made AudioContext and all guarded try/catch so a blocked context costs nothing: (1) whooshSound - a close pass shears past as bandpass-filtered noise sweeping 900-2400 Hz down to 180 Hz over 0.3 s, panned 70% to the flank the passed car was on (StereoPanner where available, mono fallback), its gain 0.10-0.32 and filter opening scaled by tightness = 1 - clearance/CLOSE_MAX; (2) chimeSound - each chain link from x2 rings two triangle notes (root + fifth) a step higher than the last, base 500 Hz x 1.19^(step-2), so you can hear which multiplier you are riding; (3) chainWarnSound - one dry 1250 Hz square tick when a live chain's bar falls under 0.9 s, once per chain episode; (4) chainBreakSound - a low 220->105 Hz falling blip when the multiplier dies.
